about: Which recordings in data/ are used for what (data/ is not in git). core: replayed by every node tools/check.mjs; library: kept for a reason, replayed with --library; a file in data/ not listed here is unsorted and not used. Numbers per recording: node tools/profile.mjs <name>. Cases: one train, a short window, one rule (node tools/cases.mjs). The core is chosen on the profile and replay numbers, with the reason written here.

slots.coveredBy: Saturday 10:00 holds the midday kind of hour in the core (SL's GPS off, the hardest replay); the weekday midday with SL's GPS on (Thu 19 Nov 11:30) is in the library: its replay is easier than Saturday's and its reporting close to the rush hours'

recordings.name: 2026-11-12T06-00-00-005Z
recordings.why: The busiest traffic recorded: 363 trains at once (most 389), 1,820 real stops, 155 silences of 5 min or more, 54 jumps. Also most pictures' fixed moment (tools/lib/browser.mjs RUSH_HOUR; the screens check moved to a recording with its routes saved, CARD_HOUR, 2026-11-17: this one's are gone at Trafikverket).

recordings.name: 2026-11-12T17-01-59-418Z
recordings.why: Evening rush with the most lateness recorded (19 % of trains 6 min or more late, 90 % of passings within 8 min) and the trains Max saw that evening (cases). Chosen over 15-30-00 (16:30, a little busier, less late): the morning already covers the busiest traffic.

recordings.name: 2026-11-11T21-45-41-004Z
recordings.why: Quiet traffic (156 trains at once), the highest share of time in silences (42 %) and of trains without a speed (37 %): silent trains moved by the timetable.

recordings.name: 2026-11-12T23-02-56-574Z
recordings.why: Night: unlike every other recording. 78 trains at once, 62 % never send a speed (mostly freight), 59 % of train time in GPS silences of 30 s or more, 22 % of trains 6 min or more late. Also the first hour with the recorder fix: no stream break.

recordings.name: 2026-11-14T09-00-00-018Z
recordings.why: Saturday daytime, but an hour with SL's GPS missing from the feed (1-2 of about 32 SL trains sent GPS; docs/night-1114/night/_night_zero.mjs), like the night and the Friday midday: so it measures "SL without GPS" more than "Saturday". 241 trains at once, 56 % never send a speed, 52 % of train time in GPS silences of 30 s or more, 8 % of trains 6 min or more late. Same profile as the Friday midday, but a harder replay: stops driven through 18.6 % (the worst of all recordings; midday 15.9 %, others 11-15 %), 90 % within 10.3 s (midday 9.4 s). It takes the midday's core place, keeping the check at 5 recordings. A Saturday with SL's GPS on is still to record. Fourth live hour with the recorder fix: no stream break.

recordings.name: 2026-11-17T15-00-00-001Z
recordings.why: The screens check's replay (tools/lib/browser.mjs CARD_HOUR, 2026-11-17): the first recording with its trains' routes saved at once (823 of 823), so the train card has its stops; a weekday rush, two hours, SL's GPS on (117 of 120 SL trains sent a speed; Sat 14 Nov 4 of 56). 361 trains at once (most 378), 32 % never send a speed, 40 % of train time in GPS silences of 30 s or more, 101 jumps, 22 % of trains 6 min or more late. One stream break each for positions and timetable, asked again at once: no gap over 20 s in the positions. Library, not core: the evening rush already has its core hour; at 137 MB the page still shows trains after 5.5 s (rush hour 4 s).

recordings.name: 2026-11-19T10-30-00-013Z
recordings.why: Weekday midday with SL's GPS on (34-38 of 34-38 SL trains sent a speed in every 10 minutes; the Friday 13 Nov midday had it off). 273 trains at once (most 306), 33.7 % never send a speed (Fri 13 Nov 57 %), 40.2 % of train time in GPS silences of 30 s or more, 40 jumps, 13.4 % of trains 6 min or more late; routes saved for all trains at once. Replays at 90 % within 5.7 s, frozen 0.4 %, stops driven through 13.4 % (Saturday's core hour: 10.3 s, 18.6 %). Library, not core: easier than Saturday's hour, and its reporting is the rush hours' with fewer trains, both already in the core.

recordings.name: 2026-11-13T10-30-00-013Z
recordings.why: Weekday midday: 273 trains at once (most 302), and unlike the rush hours 57 % of trains never send a speed (rush hours 33 %) and 52 % of train time is in GPS silences of 30 s or more (rush hours 40-41 %): many trains moving on silence and the timetable at normal traffic. Lateness low (11 % of trains 6 min or more late). Third live hour with the recorder fix: no stream break. An hour with SL's GPS missing from the feed (1-2 of about 37 SL trains sent GPS), so it measures that more than "midday". Moved to the library 2026-11-14: Saturday 10:00 is the same kind of hour with a harder replay, and took its core place.

recordings.name: 2026-11-13T04-00-00-000Z
recordings.why: First trains: the day starting up, 84 trains at once at 05:00 rising to 244 (median 179); 31 % never send a speed, 34 % of train time in GPS silences of 30 s or more, little lateness (6 % of trains 6 min or more late). Library, not core: the night already holds the quiet hours and the morning rush has more trains starting and ending (601 in all against 363 at once). Second live hour with the recorder fix: no stream break.

recordings.name: 2026-11-12T15-30-00-006Z
recordings.why: The busiest evening hour (369 trains at once, 66 jumps); a second rush hour to confirm a change on.

recordings.name: 2026-11-12T19-42-00-050Z
recordings.why: Recorded after Max saw 2567 drive through Stockholms södra (20:38, just before it started); commuter trains through Sst.

recordings.name: 2026-11-11T16-46-20-921Z
recordings.why: The first measurements in the docs (data.md) were made on it; positions only, no timetable, so no planned routes.

recordings.name: 2026-11-15T22-15-13-852Z
recordings.why: VR 2047 Stockholm C → Göteborg C diverted (Elfel) and split over three internal numbers (2047, 12015, 12016); the split-trip work (src/trip.js, fix/handover, the Herrljunga turn-round) was measured on it. 158 trains, 123 at once (profile.mjs).

cases.seen: Max, live, 2026-11-12 18:34: stopped east of Gnesta while the real train ran ~150 km/h, then raced to catch up (~700 km/h). Cause: tiny track pieces at Södermalm cut the way to Stockholm C, so it couldn't move by the timetable.

Max, live, 2026-11-12 20:38: 2567 drove through Stockholms södra without stopping (not recorded); 2556 at 18:22 is the same pattern, recorded: the real train stood ~40 s (hindsight track; its GPS repeated the platform position 18:21:56-18:23:08).
cases.fixedBy: trains: stand at the planned stops they reach (fix/dwell-at-stops; drawn 0 -> 7 s), and a standing target is braked into, not crept up to (fix/arrive-braking; 7 -> 31 s)

cases.seen: Found in the replay (U-turn hunt, 2026-11-12): GPS wobble at the standing train turned the track ahead round; the drawn train slid ~110 m back and forth at Kallhäll, 18:05.
cases.fixedBy: trains: a direction needs 20 m of movement (main, 'fix/wrong-way')

cases.seen: Found in the replay (night of 2026-11-14, wrong-branch count): coming from Strömsbro towards Gävle C the drawn train took the shortest way to a track near the station point, the other side of the yard, and slid about 340 m sideways when its report came (6 trains an hour there).
cases.fixedBy: rail-net: main tracks first for the track ahead (night/fixes-1114-main-tracks)

cases.seen: Found in the replay (night of 2026-11-14): towards Södertälje Syd the drawn train took the commuter line below the main-line station (shorter by about 140 m) and slid about 80 m sideways.
cases.fixedBy: rail-net: main tracks first for the track ahead (night/fixes-1114-main-tracks)

cases.seen: Found in the replay (night of 2026-11-14): a reported passing at Triangeln, 77 m away, was reached only the long way round Malmö (21.8 km) and the drawn train fast-forwarded along it at about 1,000 km/h (346 km/h after the report fixes of the same day; a Pågatåg runs at most 200).
cases.fixedBy: trains: a passing is used only when the way to it is at most 1.5 x the straight distance + 2 km (night/fixes-1114-main-tracks)
